newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOKYO CORN FUTURES END LOWER ON CBOT PROJECT A.
newsitem.headline: TOKYO CORN FUTURES END LOWER ON CBOT PROJECT A.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures reversed early gains to end lower on Thursday as losses on CBOT Project A led to long-liquidation from private investors, traders said.
Forecasts for wetter weather in the U.S. midwest this weekend helped push down the futures on CBOT Project A, they said.
The benchmark July 1998 contract was down 160 yen at 14,280 yen per tonne. The volume was estimated at 52,359 lots.
"Although some short-covering was detected at the opening in a correction to recent oversold conditions, sentiment was basically bearish," one trader said.
"If there is rain this weekend as expected, more losses are likely," he said.
Another trader said private investors who faced massive losses in yen-based palladium futures were looking to liquidate their longs in corn futures.
The focus is on USDA figures to be released next week.

The spot September corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was trading at $2.57-1/2 per bushel at 0853 GMT, against $2.59 at Wednesday's close. Spot August CBOT soybean futures were at $7.62-1/4 per bushel at 0853 GMT, against $7.69 at Wednesday's close.
